overview_text: History, culture, and law is an interdisciplinary major administered by the Department of History that offers students an opportunity to understand how legal systems are shaped by cultural norms and historical developments, as well as how social change has been and can be created through legal processes. After studying principles of historical method and jurisprudence, students bring to bear the interdisciplinary frameworks they have begun to develop in one of seven culturally focused concentrations: Africana studies and culture; Asian studies and culture; culture and colonialism; digital humanities; film and international cultures; gender and sexuality; and Latinx, Latin American, and Caribbean studies. HCL at Northeastern University emphasizes the study of local, regional, national, and transnational histories and cultures, as well as the comparative study of law and legal history. The program requires students to develop research skills through seminars in research methodology. The broad-based education provided by the HCL major grounds students in knowledge of the historical exchange between peoples, cultures, and societies that is key to understanding contemporary issues such as international law, the future of democracy, the nature of citizenship and rights, the origins and conduct of war, the foundations of racial and ethnic conflict and tolerance, and poverty and prosperity. At the same time, the HCL major teaches crucial skills in analytical thinking, research processes, writing, oral expression, and multimedia presentation.
